Output: Cash assistance and financial inclusion programs targeting women implemented. Indicator: The government disbursed $0.44 billion total of cash grants to 12 million families under the Kifalat Program. Achievement: 14830000 Progress/Status: As of February 2021: The initial target set by the Federal Government was to disburse Rs. 144 billion among 12 million beneficiaries under Ehsaas Emergency Cash Programme (EECP) rather than Ehsaas Kifalat Programme. However, beneficiaries of Ehsaas Kifalat Programme were also included in the EECP. Later the target was revised to disbursement of Rs. 203 billion to 16.9 million beneficiaries (including Rs. 8.4 billion funded by Punjab Government for around 0.7 million additional beneficiaries of Punjab). Out of these, cash assistance of Rs. 179.27 billion has been disbursed to around 14.83 million beneficiaries under EECP as of 02-02-2021.
It seems that 7.5 million new beneficiaries mentioned in the indicator actually pertain to 7.5 million beneficiaries of Category-2 & 3 of Ehsaas Emergency Cash Program (EECP) (excluding 4.5 million regular beneficiaries of Ehsaas Kifalat Programme), initially targeted for 12 million total beneficiaries. As apprised above, the target under EECP was later revised to 16.9 million beneficiaries. Out of 16.9 million, around 11.89 million beneficiaries were new beneficiaries. Out of 11.89 million, around 10.18 million beneficiaries have been disbursed as of 22 Feb 2021. Out of these 10.18 million beneficiaries, 3,349,789 were women, 6,828,584 were men and 26 were transgender. It is pertinent to mention that as per policy approved by BISP Board, preference was given to ever married male of the family with valid CNIC, keeping in view the emergency situation and lockdowns across the country. If no such male was available in the family then ever married woman of the same family with valid CNIC was declared recipient of cash assistance. Data Source: Federal budget statements

Output: Cash assistance and financial inclusion programs targeting women implemented. Indicator: Under the Financial Inclusion Strategy, at least 6 million female beneficiaries received money through their bank accounts. (2019 baseline: 4.5 million) Progress/Status: As of February 2021: It is apprised that all beneficiaries of Ehsaas Kifalat as well as Ehsaas Emergency Cash Programme (EECP) have been disbursed payments through Limited Mandate Accounts (LMA). However, as per Financial Inclusion Strategy approved by the BISP Board, Mobile Wallets (BB Saving Accounts) of all regular Kifalat beneficiaries will also be opened which will be linked with their LMAs. Beneficiaries will be given the choice to either withdraw their amounts through LMAs or to transfer the same to linked BB Saving Accounts. Moreover, beneficiaries will also be imparted Financial Literacy as part of Financial Inclusion Strategy. BISP has recently designed and launched a Pilot for Mobile Wallet & Financial Literacy Programme in 13 Districts across the country. After evaluating the pilot, a detailed road map and action plan will be prepared and submitted for Board's approval to launch the project in all remaining Districts. Data Source: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) database, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) annual report, and independent evaluation through surveys. Actual value:
